newsitem.title: GERMANY: Film about Larry Flynt wins Berlin Golden Bear.
newsitem.headline: Film about Larry Flynt wins Berlin Golden Bear.

text.p: "The People vs Larry Flynt", a controversial film about the American pornography publishing king, won the top "Golden Bear" prize on Monday for best film at the 47th Berlin film festival.
Jury president Jack Lang, France's former Culture Minister, told a news conference the film by Czech-born director Milos Forman had won top honours.

The film, which won two Oscar nominations this month but has stirred controversy in several countries, depicts the tumultuous life of publisher Larry Flynt, a school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful magazine Hustler in 1973.

The jury awarded Silver Bear prizes to Juliette Binoche for best actress for her performance in the acclaimed World War Two romance "The English Patient" and to Leonardo di Caprio for his role in "William Shakespeare's Romeo and Julia".
French star Binoche plays a French-Canadian nurse who helps a man suffering from amnesia in "The English Patient". Di Caprio plays the male lead in "Romeo and Julia".

"The English Patient", which has received 12 Academy Award nominations, and "The People vs Larry Flynt" were both expected to win awards in Berlin, Europe's second most important film festival after Cannes in May.

After "The People vs Larry Flynt" made its international premiere last week in Berlin, Forman rejected criticism from feminists who criticised the film and said his film was about freedom of the press and not pornography.

"Pornography is the price to pay for freedom of the press," said Forman. "Freedom of the press is more important than elections or free markets. Elections and free markets can be manipulated, as Hitler did. But a free press cannot."
Aside from a few bare-breast scenes, there are no other sexually explicit moments in "The People vs Larry Flynt."
Forman said on Monday he had decided to withdraw posters advertising the film in France after complaints that they offended Christians.

French judges last week refused to ban the posters after pleas by a group of Roman Catholics and a right-wing association that they were an infringement on religious freedom. They show actor Woody Harrelson, arms outstretched in a crucifix-like pose, wearing only briefs made of the Stars and Stripes flag, against a backdrop of a woman's bikini-clad loins.

"Given the incomprehension prompted by the poster, the attacks and the threats against distributors and the harnessing (of the issue) by various politico-religious associations, I have asked Columbia Pictures in a pacifying gesture...to withdraw this poster, which it has accepted," Forman said.

"Its design was meant to reflect the satirical treatment of the themes of the film: fake patriotism, hypocritical piety, the use of nudity as a commodity, and to display the freedom we enjoy in the United States to examine such subjects," he added in a statement. The film spotlights Flynt's legal battles against America's conservative Christian leader, the Rev. Jerry Falwell, and others opposed to his magazine because of its obscenity. Flynt, now 54, was paralysed from the waist down after an unknown assailant shot him while he was leaving a courthouse in 1978.
After defeating Falwell in the Supreme Court, Flynt said: "If they will protect a scumbag like me, then they'll protect all of you."

Harrelson, who portrays Flint, won a best actor nomination in Hollywood recently for his convincing performance and Forman was nominated for another best directing Oscar. He has already has won Academy Awards for "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" and "Amadeus". The film also stars Courtney Love, a rock-star turned actress.
The "Golden Bear" for "The People vs Larry Flynt" was a surprise for some of the 1,100 journalists, many of whom had picked "The English Patient" for top honours.
